segments.text: Next up are physical incidents, which are comprised of fires, slips and falls, and musculoskeletal hazards.
segments.zh: 接下来是物理事件，包括火灾、滑倒和跌倒，以及肌肉骨骼危害。

segments.text: If a fire starts, get everyone out. No hesitation.
segments.zh: 如果起火了，让所有人都撤出去。不要犹豫。

segments.text: Once the area is clear, if it's a small fire, grab the extinguisher and use the pass method.
segments.zh: 一旦该区域的人员撤空，如果是小火，就拿起灭火器，使用 PASS 方法。

segments.text: Pull, aim, squeeze, and sweep.
segments.zh: 拔、瞄、压、扫。

segments.text: Fires are classified into different types.
segments.zh: 火灾分为不同的类型。

segments.text: Class A, ordinary combustibles like paper and wood.
segments.zh: A 类，普通可燃物，比如纸和木材。

segments.text: Class B, flammable liquids.
segments.zh: B 类，易燃液体。

segments.text: Class C, electrical.
segments.zh: C 类，电气火灾。

segments.text: Class D, metal fires.
segments.zh: D 类，金属火灾。

segments.text: Be sure to use the correct extinguisher for the type of fire.
segments.zh: 一定要针对火灾类型使用正确的灭火器。

segments.text: If it's getting out of hand or you're unsure, don't take any chances.
segments.zh: 如果火势失控，或者你没有把握，就不要冒险。

segments.text: Call for help.
segments.zh: 呼叫求助。

segments.text: After it's out, double check to make sure nothing can reignite.
segments.zh: 火扑灭后，再仔细检查，确保没有东西会复燃。

segments.text: Slips happen before you know it.
segments.zh: 滑倒往往在你还没反应过来时就发生了。

segments.text: If you fall, don't jump up right away.
segments.zh: 如果你摔倒了，不要马上跳起来。

segments.text: Take a second to see if you're okay.
segments.zh: 花一点时间看看自己是否还好。

segments.text: If something hurts or you're feeling off, get help.
segments.zh: 如果哪里疼或者感觉不对劲，就寻求帮助。

segments.text: If you're fine, stand up slowly with support.
segments.zh: 如果你没事，就在有支撑的情况下慢慢站起来。

segments.text: Then clean up whatever caused the fall so no one else gets hurt.
segments.zh: 然后把导致摔倒的东西清理干净，免得别人受伤。

segments.text: Musculoskeletal hazards are the aches that sneak up on you after repetitive work.
segments.zh: 肌肉骨骼危害是重复性工作后悄悄找上你的那些酸痛。

segments.text: Whether it's your back, neck, or wrist, don't brush it off.
segments.zh: 无论是背部、颈部还是手腕，都不要不当回事。

segments.text: Stop, stretch, and adjust your setup.
segments.zh: 停下来，伸展一下，调整你的工作台设置。

segments.text: If the pain keeps coming back, talk to someone about making changes and see a doctor before it turns into something bigger.
segments.zh: 如果疼痛反复出现，就找人谈谈如何做出改变，并在它发展成更大的问题之前去看医生。

segments.text: NFPA 45 is your guide to making sure fire safety is solid in the lab.
segments.zh: NFPA 45 是确保实验室消防安全牢靠的指南。

segments.text: But don't just stop there. Local fire codes matter too.
segments.zh: 但不要仅止于此。当地的消防规范也很重要。

segments.text: So make sure you're on top of those.
segments.zh: 所以一定要掌握这些规范。

segments.text: Cutting corners here isn't worth the risk.
segments.zh: 在这方面偷工减料，不值得冒这个险。

segments.text: Now, when it comes to keeping your body in check, OSHA's got your back with regulations like 29 CFR 1910.900,
segments.zh: 现在，说到照顾好你的身体，OSHA 有 29 CFR 1910.900 之类的法规为你提供保障，

segments.text: which focuses on preventing musculoskeletal disorders through better ergonomics.
segments.zh: 它侧重于通过更好的人体工学来预防肌肉骨骼疾病。

segments.text: And don't forget, standards like OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1450 for lab safety and 29 CFR 1910.38A for emergency plans are key to staying safe and compliant.
segments.zh: 还有别忘了，像 OSHA 29 CFR 1910.1450 实验室安全标准和 29 CFR 1910.38A 应急计划标准，都是保持安全与合规的关键。

segments.text: Get familiar with these and you'll be in good shape.
segments.zh: 熟悉这些标准，你就没问题了。
